Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-15
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SRE); Maya Hernandez, Liam O'Connor, Dinesh Patel (Cobalt)
Links referenced: offline bundle spec (link: https://redwood.example/offline-bundle-spec), driver matrix (link: drive://redwood/driver-matrix), pilot checklist (link: s3://cobalt/pilot-checklist)

Summary (auto):
Redwood walked through the on-prem air-gapped delivery flow: signed bundle generation, verification steps for Cobalt's offline environment, and GPU driver/kernel tuning tradeoffs for A100 vs H100. Customer raised questions about offline license activation, HSM/KMS integration, checksum verification, and required libc/kernel versions. Agreed action items and timeline.

Topics: artifact signing, bundle delivery, offline activation flow, driver/cuda compatibility, KV cache warmup, batching/latency impact, quantization caveats, transfer media options (USB/airgap broker).

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, im alex kim, AE on the account. priya and samir from our side will cover the technical bits. maya, liam, dinesh, thanks for making time.
[00:18] Maya: yeah thanks, lots on our plate. we're onboarding a few models and need a clean offline install path. main asks: signed binaries, offline activation, and minimal driver impact on perf.
[00:32] Priya: great, i'll run through the bundle flow first and then we can dig into kernel/driver tuning. forgive me if i mumbles, i'll try to keep timestamps.
[00:47] Priya: so the offline bundle is a tar.gz with runtime binaries, model shards, and a metadata.json. everything's GPG-signed and we produce a detached sig and an sha256sum file. in air-gapped env you verify the sig with our public key, and optionally re-check checksum against the manifest.
[01:10] Liam: can you clarify the signing key lifecycle? do we rotate keys frequently? we're strict about attestations and we want to pin a key in our HSM.
[01:24] Priya: yes, we support key pinning. by default bundles are signed by a Redwood release key; for enterprise/private installs we can have the bundle signed by a customer-managed key—redwood provides tooling to produce the tar and sign locally if you run the packaging step. we also emit an attestation blob for the release build id.
[01:42] Dinesh: ok, and how does offline activation work? our SOC requires no outbound calls from air-gapped hosts.
[01:51] Alex: two modes: 1) offline activation codes — short-lived activation token you paste into the bundle installer which we validate when you later connect to our license server, or 2) enterprise perpetual token: we provide signed license files that the runtime validates locally against the embedded public cert. both support HSM-stored keys.
[02:16] Maya: the perpetual token sounds preferable. what's the revocation story if a host is decommissioned?
[02:25] Priya: we issue revocation lists periodically. for air-gapped you can upload a CRL as part of your offline maintenance pack, or we can provide signed revocation manifests you can apply. we also support short-term lease tokens if you prefer temporary activation.
[02:40] Liam: switching gears to drivers: our infra is mixed, some racks with A100 80GB, some with H100. we need a concrete compatibility matrix — CUDA, cuDNN, kernel module versions — and any special kernel flags.
[02:56] Samir: yeah, that's where we see most of the field variance. big callouts: CUDA 11 vs 12 differences, NV driver 535 vs 550, and the h100 firmware quirks. we recommend a tested driver set per model family; i'll share the matrix after. note: quantized int8 paths may require a newer driver/toolkit on H100.
[03:20] Liam: do we require DKMS or a static module? our security team doesn't like DKMS on hardened kernels.
[03:28] Priya: we support both. static prebuilt modules are included in the bundle for supported kernel minor versions; for other kernels we provide source and a DKMS flow. we also provide a fallback user-space provider that avoids kernel modules at some perf cost.
[03:45] Maya: fallback for perf cost — can you quantify? like 10%? 30%?
[03:50] Priya: rough numbers: user-space fallback adds ~12-20% latency on tail calls for small batch sizes; throughput hits vary by model. it's not linear. you'll see bigger gaps on models that rely on fused kernels and Ampere/Hopper-specific intrinsics.
[04:08] Liam: KV cache warmup — for our use cases warm starts are critical. how do you recommend pre-warming in offline mode?
[04:16] Samir: we have a prefix cache export option: you can precompute KV slices using the same tokenizer and seed prompts, bundle them, and load them at runtime. the bundle includes a KV manifest that maps model shard offsets to cache files. note: these are large — plan for network/storage transfer.
[04:36] Dinesh: that raises transport questions. we can't accept direct S3 endpoints. what's the supported media?
[04:44] Priya: supported options: encrypted USB drives with signed manifests, air-gap appliance (we've used Aspera or rclone behind an approved transfer gateway before), and one-off physical shipment of HDDs. we provide verification scripts that run the GPG and sha256 checks locally.
[05:02] Maya: any rules about libc or glibc versions? we've had problems with older distros.
[05:09] Samir: yes, minimal supported glibc is 2.27 for our compiled runtime; we test on RHEL8/CentOS8 and Ubuntu 20.04+. older distros will need the static-linked runtime or a containerized shim.
[05:24] Liam: container shim in air-gapped? we prefer not to rely on docker daemons.
[05:29] Priya: we support OCI images that can be run with crun or runc, and rootless options. when containers aren't allowed we provide a system-wide installer that lays down files in /opt/redwood and a service unit.
[05:44] Alex: quick note on quantization — int8 offers big cost wins but watch for regressions on rare tokens; we recommend evaluation suites and not enabling int8 by default in early pilots.
[05:58] Maya: do you supply quantization profiles per model?
[06:03] Priya: yes, we ship recommended profiles and a conversion tool. the bundle includes both float and quantized kernel blobs where supported. sometimes on H100 the int4/int8 codepath needs a newer CUDA/driver to be stable.
[06:20] Liam: can you talk about smart batching and latency SLOs? in an on-prem deployment we need predictable tail latency.
[06:29] Samir: the runtime has continuous batching with policy knobs. for tail latency you can set a max batch size and a max latency cap which forces immediate flush. we also support priority routing so hot routes skip batching. for predictable tails we recommend small batch sizes (2-8 tokens) and aggressive KV caching for prefixes.
[06:50] Maya: what's the token accounting when you preload KV cache? are those tokens billed or charged?
[06:56] Alex: for dedicated/offline customers billing is via committed capacity; cache preloads are not double-billed. for hosted they show as storage/transfer events. we'll clarify in the contract.
[07:12] Dinesh: security — network egress is disallowed. please outline any telemetry or callbacks the runtime attempts out of the box.
[07:21] Priya: default runtime phone-home is off in the offline bundle. we have an ops-mode where you can permit telemetry via an explicit toggle. license validation in perpetual mode is local. we do produce logs that can optionally be pushed, but that requires customer-approved transfer steps.
[07:38] Liam: about kernel tuning — any sysctl knobs or hugepages recommendations?
[07:44] Samir: big recommendations: disable CPU C-states for latency-sensitive nodes, set vm.swappiness low, enable hugepages (2MB) for model shards memory mapping, and tune network interrupt affinities if you're using RDMA. we'll include a sysctl script in the bundle.
[08:05] Maya: one of our blockers is verification of the bundle on our side. can you provide a short checklist we can give our security ops?
[08:12] Priya: yes — checklist includes: verify GPG signature, sha256sum, confirm bundle manifest matches release ID, check module signatures for kernel modules, run the runtime in dry-run mode to print hashes of loaded libs. i'll attach the checklist doc.
[08:30] Alex: question for liam: what's your target pilot timeline?
[08:35] Liam: we want to start a pilot by Jan 12, 2026 and have a production gate by end of Q1 — security sign-off is the long pole.
[08:45] Alex: ok that lines up. we'll prioritize the driver matrix and the offline license templates for the next week.
[08:53] Dinesh: hypothetical: if we need to rotate runtime signing keys and we only have physical access windows every quarter, can we automate with your tooling?
[09:03] Priya: yes, we have an offline key rotation flow: generate new keypair in your HSM, produce a rotation manifest signed by old key, apply locally. we can run through it in a dry exercise.
[09:17] Maya: wanted to re-raise the KV cache prewarming size — do you have compression options for kv slices?
[09:23] Samir: we gzip and optionally delta-compress similar slices; for large prefix sets we recommend zstd for better compression/CPU tradeoff. we also support chunked load so the runtime streams cache slices as needed to avoid large spikes.
[09:40] Liam: any gotchas running on H100 with mixed topology? we've seen hangs when multiple processes try to share NVLINK.
[09:48] Samir: for H100 we recommend exclusive process mode per GPU for deterministic perf; also set NCCL to tree-based transports and pin numa nodes. we'll document sample systemd units that enforce cpuset and gpu affinity.
[10:08] Maya: can you include an example systemd unit and tune file?
[10:12] Priya: yes i'll include those in the bundle under examples/.
[10:20] Alex: ok wrapping — recap of action items. Priya will send bundle signing checklist and driver matrix. Alex will send licensing template and pricing. Maya to confirm transport method and hardware list. we'll schedule a follow-up on-site readiness call week of Dec 22.
[10:40] Liam: thanks everyone. small note: please cc security distro team on the checklist.
[10:47] Dinesh: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
